chapter: The Raeburn band: people and touring
title: Raeburn alumni: Kluger, Savitt, Benny Harris, Trummy Young, Diz and Bird
summary: Handy recalls trumpet section players and stars like Gillespie and Parker who passed through.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: How about Irv Kluger?
Irv Kluger, the drummer?
Was he on the band during one of your times? I think he was.
He was there at one period. I don't remember too much about him, but he seemed to be all right. I don't have--I can't recall too much about Irv other than he
was there. The lead trumpet player was Beech--who was the lead player?
Pinky.
Tommy Allison?
He played second.
Pinky Savitt.
That's him, Pinky Savitt played lead.
And Benny Harris?
That was for a small period of time, Benny Harris. He wasn't there-- he was there in the early days.
There were an awful lot of "stars" that went through that band. Trummy Young was on the band.
Trummy, Diz. Even Bird was there for a date or two.
I didn't know that.
Yeah, in New York I think Bird played a couple of dates. He might have been out there at the Palisades before the
Were you on the band when Diz came out?
Diz was there when I was with the band; yeah.
Was he really a regular or did he just show up at times?
Diz? He wasn't a regular, but he would do a week with us; he was in and out.
Was he a good technical player in those days, in addition to being an extraordinary soloist, but he played in tune and played the book well and cooperated as a section player?

He was a marvelous musician; right. He was more than just a soloist, he was really all you could ask of a musician. He fulfills the responsibility of whatever he's asked to do. If he's asked to play solo or backup, he does it well.
How about Bird, was
he a section player too?
I don't remember too much about Bird in the band. Who knew in those days that you had to pay absolute attention to everything this guy does. Didn't know, just didn't know.
